request.spec:
A claim may carry an external reference: a text on the claim form (surrounding spaces removed),
shown on the claim. A reference already used on the sheet, comparing without regard to case, is
refused with an error on the form, and nothing is saved; a blank reference is no reference. A
pasted line gives it at the end of its note as ` #<reference>` (a space, a hash, the reference:
that part is the reference, not part of the note), checked the same way and refusing the whole
paste on a repeat, within the paste too. CLAIM_ADDED gains ref=<reference> at its end when one was
given.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims can now carry an external reference, and all 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`. I only changed endpoint comments after that run, so it still holds.

**What it does**
- **Storage:** a new migration, `V51__claim_ref.sql`, adds a `ref` column to claims. A claim with no reference stores nothing there.
- **Claim form:** there's a new reference field (`claim-form-ref`), and the claim shows its reference (`claim-ref`). Spaces around it are removed, and a blank one counts as no reference.
- **Repeats:** a reference already used on the sheet, ignoring case, is refused with an error on the form and nothing is saved. When you edit a claim, its own reference isn't counted as a repeat.
- **Paste:** a line's note is trimmed first. If it then ends in ` #<reference>`, that part becomes the reference and is taken off the note. A reference that repeats one on the sheet, or another line in the same paste, refuses the whole paste.
- **Audit:** `CLAIM_ADDED` ends with `ref=<reference>` when the claim has one. `CLAIM_EDITED` and the other records are unchanged.

**Behaviours to know about**
- A paste line like `Ben,2.00,2026-03-01, #inv-4` gets no reference. After trimming, the note is just `#inv-4`, with no space before the hash, so it stays as the note. The test expects exactly this.
- If a note has more than one ` #`, only the last one counts: `a #b #c` gives reference `c` and note `a #b`.
- Splitting a claim doesn't copy its reference to the new claim, since a copy would be a repeat.
- Repeats are only checked in the app, not by a database rule. If two people saved the same reference at the same instant, both could get through. A unique index on the sheet plus the reference, ignoring case, would close that gap if you want it.
